narrative.overview: The whole page is one pane of shop-window glass at night: deep navy with a single soft diagonal reflection. On the glass, sign painter's lettering in Ultra is gilded with burnished leaf, ringed in red and stepped with a dark-red block shade. Behind it hang real objects: one white application card, a red porcelain sign, an enamel plaque. Density is low; objects carry their own materials through inset rims and soft drop shadows. Brand inks are the logo's navy and red; gold is the sign painter's metal, never a flat UI fill.
keyCharacteristics: Night glass ground with one diagonal reflection
Gilded Ultra lettering: leaf, red ring, block shade
One white card, which is the live form, hung at -0.8deg
Porcelain enamel plates for motto and steps
Barlow body, Barlow Condensed labels, Yellowtail sign phrases

rules.name: The Metal Is Not Paint Rule
rules.body: Gold appears as leaf, pinstripe, tick or hairline; never as a surface fill.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Red and navy are the only chromatic inks besides gold; no added accent hues.

rules.name: The Lettering Is Painted Rule
rules.body: Ultra on glass is always gilded with all three layers; on enamel or card it is flat navy or red.

rules.name: The One Flourish Rule
rules.body: Yellowtail only for the card's sign phrase, success state and footer tagline; never above section headings.

rules.name: The One Pane Rule
rules.body: The glass runs unbroken from header to final call; objects hang on it instead of section bands.

rules.name: The Single Reflection Rule
rules.body: Exactly one diagonal reflection on the glass; no glows, noise or extra light.

rules.name: The Shade Belongs To Letters Rule
rules.body: Hard offset shadows only as block shade on Ultra lettering; objects cast soft shadows.

dos: Do gild every Ultra heading on the glass with leaf, red ring and block shade.
Do hang new content as objects on the one pane with soft shadows and inset rims.
Do use double rules for dividers: red on light surfaces, gold-dim on glass.
Do keep the application card the only card and keep the form in the first viewport.
Do use stroke icons only where they do a job (tick, arrow, lock, alert).
Do honor reduced motion: glint, transitions and smooth scroll off.
donts: Don't build grids of icon cards or tiles.
Don't give non-interactive plates the gold pinstripe; it means press.
Don't add a second reflection, glow or texture to the glass.
Don't fill surfaces with gold or add a new accent hue.
Don't stack small labels or script lines above section headings.
Don't alter, recolor or crop the CAA logo or set it on the glass without its plate.
